newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-SEIZINGER CONTINUES TO DOMINATE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SEIZINGER CONTINUES TO DOMINATE.

text.p: Olympic champion Katja Seizinger of Germany continued to dominate downhill training at the Alpine skiing world championships, clocking the fastest time in practice on Wednesday.

Showing no lingering effects from the mild concussion she sustained in a high speed spill in the last downhill prior to the championships, Seizinger zipped down the Kandahar Banchetta course in a time of one minute, 41.83 seconds.

"It was a little bumpy because of the super-G yesterday but other than that it was good," said Seizinger, the reigning overall World Cup champion. "This isn't a really difficult downhill so the one who makes the fewest mistakes will win.
"I think you'll need an almost perfect run to win on this downhill."
And after three days on the course, Seizinger has been just that -- almost perfect.
She posted the fastest time in opening training on Monday and claimed silver in the super-G, run on the same Kandahar Banchetta piste, on Tuesday.
While Seizinger's name is a familiar sight atop the training results, American Hilary Lindh's appearance behind her with a time of 1:42.58, was not expected.

After a slow start to the season, Lindh appears to be finally rediscovering the form that earned her a bronze medal at last year's championships in Sierra Nevada, Spain. She recorded her best two results of her season in the last two downhills coming into the championships, including a fourth place on February 1 in Laax, Switzerland.

"I think the race will be a real crap shoot," said Lindh, who will carry American medal hopes into Saturday's race with reigning champion Picabo Street out for the season with torn knee ligaments. "I mean there a few favourites like Seizinger and Kostner but I think it's pretty wide open."
Switzerland's Heidi Zurbriggen, leader of the World Cup downhill standings, had the day's third best time of 1:42.72 followed closely by Germany's Regina Haeusl with 1:42.75.
Isolde Kostner, who gave Italy its third gold medal with a victory in the super-G, crossed 12th in 1:43.06 but hit the breaks the final 100 metres and coasted across the finish line.
Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg, who has been battling a cold the last few days, finished well back in 24th place and rushed from the finish area back to bed as soon as she completed her run.
"It's a little better," sniffed Wiberg, runaway leader of the overall World Cup standings. "I still have a cough but at least the fever has gone.
